Emergency Aid: ingestion experiments

Chunking reduces temporary data, but retained state can still grow. I measured it before choosing the next change.

Protocol

Compare under declared conditions.

Python → Pandas → asyncpg COPY → PostgreSQL. Each run starts with a newly migrated database; RSS measures the Python process, not the database.

100-thousand-row chunks, one warm-up, and three measured runs per scenario; tables use medians.

Throughput and memory

Memory diagnosis

Fixed chunks did not prevent growing state.

182 → 750 MiBPost-cleanup RSS: ~568 MiB more over 50 chunks.
r ≈ 0.991Strong association with retained IDs; not isolated causality.
3 runsSame direction, one environment.

At 5 million rows, sets hold about 5.44 million IDs. The descriptive fit is ~107 MiB per million IDs; RSS also includes runtime and buffers.

Supported conclusion: memory is not bounded by chunk size. Hypothesis: global sets contribute to retention. Next test: staging-based deduplication, repeating checkpoints and comparing the post-cleanup curve.

Limits and next steps

What still needs measurement.

Polars/PySpark and index or staging gains remain unmeasured. SQL benchmarking needs cache control and EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

The 50-chunk trajectory is the relevant retention test; DataFrame estimates are not physical RSS.
